FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Hamburg’s superb home form will be put to the test by a Bayern Munich side who proved in midweek that it may take them time to adapt to life without Harry Kane.

Match News and Current Form

Hamburg need to bounce back to form quickly after suffering a 4-0 defeat to Werder Bremen last time out. That was already the sixth time across all competitions this term that the Red Shorts have lost by a 2+ goal margin and their hefty defeat means they have conceded 24 times in just ten Bundesliga outings, the third-most in the division. A return to Volksparkstadion, where Merlin Polzin’s men have won three consecutive top-flight outings for the first time since their promotion in 2025, should provide a confidence boost, but a record of four defeats from as many matches against teams who start this round in the top seven should be enough to keep them grounded, even if all four losses did come on the road.

Bayern Munich’s 22-match unbeaten run (W14, D8) came to an end with a shock 2-1 defeat to Lille in Europe on Wednesday. That result continued a mildly underwhelming start to the campaign for Vincent Kompany’s side, who have their lowest points haul at this stage in four years after being knocked off top spot in the Bundesliga following a 1-1 draw against Cologne in the last round. They’d be forgiven for expecting to get back in the win column on the road, with their current streak of 31 away league matches without defeat the second longest in the club’s history (W23, D8).

Head-to-Head History

Hamburg have lost more matches to Bayern Munich (75) than any other team, with their winless run in H2Hs stretching back 21 games to 2009 (D4, L17).

Win Probability
Opta by StatsPerform
Hot Stats and Streaks

Hamburg have led a joint-league low one Bundesliga game at half-time this season (HT: D6, L3).

Hamburg’s last six Bundesliga fixtures have been level at the break.

Only one of Bayern’s ten league games this term was goalless at half-time.

No team is averaging more corners per game than Bayern Munich (8.2) ahead of this round.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Hamburg’s Albert Grønbæk has scored three of his last four goals after half-time and is unbeaten across the last 16 games he has netted in for club and country (W13, D3). No Bundesliga player has won more tackles than Dayot Upamecano’s 21 ahead of this round, including at least two in five of his last six league outings.

Alexander Røssing-Lelesiit could return for Hamburg, but Miro Muheim is out. Bayern Munich remain without Harry Kane and Michael Olise is a doubt.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

The visitors’ defensive woes suggest they may concede, so both teams to score and over 2.5 goals could be worth a look.

Author: Matt Jones
